title: Comparison of Metadata Catalog Schemas for Cross-Border Health Dataset Discovery
content: Introduction: The European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation (EU) 2025/327 requires Member States to establish national health dataset catalogs feeding into the HealthData@EU infrastructure. While the detailed technical specifications for catalog content are currently being developed through HealthDCAT-AP and forthcoming implementing acts, several national and domain-specific health data infrastructures have already established metadata catalogs based on (Health)DCAT-AP and related profiles. These early implementations provide a valuable opportunity to assess emerging convergence, metadata alignment challenges, and identify practical requirements for future harmonization. Objectives: In this paper, we compare a set of independently developed metadata catalog schemas in use across European health data infrastructures to identify areas of structural and semantic convergence and divergence. This aims to provide a basis for alignment consistent with the emerging HealthDCAT-AP specification. Methods: This work was initiated at the SWAT4HCLS 2026 BioHackathon, where representatives of the participating infrastructures jointly manually mapped their schemas, and continued through extended collaborative efforts. A total of eleven schemas, health-related metadata catalogs and application profiles, were compared along three axes: classes, properties and value sets. Results: The study shows that the schemas align well with DCAT-AP, and especially requirements of the HealthDCAT-AP for the health-specific schemas, though there are some divergences and expected extensions. For aligned content, we illustrate the practical payoff of these alignments with federated SPARQL queries enabled at each level. Conclusions: The national metadata schemas provide a solid foundation towards enabling interoperable metadata discovery, while complying with the EHDS regulation. The necessary alignments and suggestions for extensions of studied schemas have been outlined, communicated and are being discussed on the national level. Beyond the technical findings, this work established a cross-community forum for alignment, knowledge exchange, and coordinated evolution of metadata specifications. Maintaining such collaboration will be essential as HealthDCAT-AP and related EHDS requirements continue to mature.
